Fix segfault in large packets
body:
The segfault occurs due to a signed integer overflow (it becomes negative).
The integer overflow happens when the size of a received PostgreSQL protocol packet exceeds 0x80000000 (2 GB).

In the PostgreSQL wire protocol, the packet size is specified as a 4-byte integer, which theoretically allows sending packets up to 4 GB in size.
However, in practice, the Postgres server allocates memory blocks of up to 1 GB:
```
#define MaxAllocSize    ((Size) 0x3fffffff)
```
When receiving a packet, the server checks its length value, and if it exceeds 1 GB (0x3fffffff), it stops processing the packet and returns an error:
```
invalid message length
```
Therefore, to fix the segfault, it was decided to add a handler that ensures the packet size does not exceed 0x80000000 (2 GB).

title: Missing floating-point register preservation in ARM64 context switching may cause data corruption under high compiler optimization levels
body:
The current aarch64 context switching implementation (context_swap_aarch64.S) only preserves general-purpose registers (x8, x16-x30) but omits floating-point registers (d8-d15). 
For example, after Coroutine A stores floating-point computation results in register d9 and switches to Coroutine B, the d9 register still contains the value left by Coroutine A. When the compiler allocates variables for Coroutine B, it may incorrectly assume that the d9 register has an initial value of 0 and use it for variable initialization, causing the variable to be assigned an incorrect initial value (which is actually Coroutine A's computation result).

title: send signal in soft oom state
Odyssey picks pg_srand48 from Postgres instead of Machinarium
body:
`pg_erand48`, `pg_lrand48`, `pg_srand48` are defined in [pg_rand48.c](https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/master/third_party/machinarium/sources/pg_rand48.c). These functions are also present in Postgres, though they were removed in Postgres 15 release.

The declaration in machinarium: `void pg_srand48(long seed, unsigned short *_rand48_seed)`
The declaration in Postgres: `extern void pg_srand48(long seed);`

**Note that Postgres declaration doesn't accept the extra parameter that Machinarium's implementation does**

When we build Odyssey with Postgres version <= 14, these functions are picked from Postgres instead of Machinarium. This is because when linking we specify Postgres libraries first and then specify Machinarium. This leads to functions from Postgres getting first priority with the static linker.

This can lead to many issues since the Postgres function does something very different than what Machinarium expects:

https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/8bd0ada761630bd948975cf3e0bdfa7850a9c8c3/third_party/machinarium/sources/lrand48.c#L21-L49

Here, `pg_srand48` is called passing `prng_seed` which ends up calling Postgres function. The variable will be stored in `%rsi` but the function doesn't have any expectations for that register. This could end up quite messy with optimizations.

Side note: this function is present in `libpgport.a`

```bash
08:42 ~ $ nm /usr/pgsql-14/lib/libpgport.a | grep pg_srand48
0000000000000127 t .annobin_pg_srand48.end
0000000000000103 t .annobin_pg_srand48.start
0000000000000110 T pg_srand48
08:42 ~ $ nm /usr/pgsql-15/lib/libpgport.a | grep pg_srand48
```

title: Missing calls to od_route_signal causing clients to remain queued in od_router_attach()?
body:
Hello Team, 

We're having some issues around the queueing semantics for incoming clients. Specifically, it seems like there are fewer usages of `od_route_signal()` than there should be? 
For context:
- `od_route_wait()` is called once during `od_router_attach()` if a client fails to immediately get a backend slot (`router.c:929`):
https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/8bd0ada761630bd948975cf3e0bdfa7850a9c8c3/sources/router.c#L926-L929 
- `od_route_signal()` is called once at the end of `od_router_detach()` if there are any queued clients (in `router.c:1040`):
https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/8bd0ada761630bd948975cf3e0bdfa7850a9c8c3/sources/router.c#L1039-L1042
- At the start of `od_router_attach()`, we enqueue the current client in the pool queue to (at `router.c:857`).
https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/8bd0ada761630bd948975cf3e0bdfa7850a9c8c3/sources/router.c#L857-L858
- Finally, upon successful attach, we return `OD_ROUTER_OK` on line 989. 
-  However, if attach fails (lines 852, 875, 917, 931 or 943), we return from `od_router_attach` with the corresponding failure. In at least some of these cases, the caller of `od_router_attach()` doesn't seem to call `od_route_signal()`.
    - See, for example, calls to `od_frontend_attach()`
    - Consider error handling in the call stack: `... -> od_frontend_setup() -> od_frontend_setup_params() -> od_frontend_attach() -> od_frontend_attach_to_endpoint() -> od_router_attach() (returning OD_ROUTER_ERROR)`, which would lead to calling `od_frontend_cleanup()` with the status passed as `OD_ETTACH`, which has no associated `od_route_signal()` call at `frontend.c:2405`. 

In essence, shouldn't `od_route_signal()` be called for every error handling path from `od_router_attach()` because we eventually unset the client from the client pool, so we need to wake up a queued client if it is waiting when the current client hits an error. 

The above is our current understanding of a potential issue. It is possible we are missing some invariant that prevents the mentioned scenario or that we are misunderstanding the intended code flow. In either case, please correct me if I am wrong.
Thanks

title: Potential dangling pointer in od_backend_connect_to
body:
In the code below in `od_backend_connect_to`, we free `io` pointer and return.
https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/8bd0ada761630bd948975cf3e0bdfa7850a9c8c3/sources/backend.c#L311-L318

This causes `server->io.io` to be a dangling pointer, pointing to freed up memory. This can cause issues when we try to access this pointer when doing cleanup after this error. I believe we should set this to `NULL` after `free`ing it atleast.

title: fix cron stop (fix data race, replace mutex with wait flag)
body:
1. There is a data race in cron (`cron->online`). It was detected by ThreadSanitizer (see #901). 
2. The current implementation uses a mutex in `od_cron` and `od_cron_stop`. This approach is inefficient (because the mutex is provided by `pthreads`) and unclear (the mutex is never unlocked).

This pull request addresses both of these issues. It makes `cron->online` an atomic variable and replaces the mutex with a `wait_flag`.

Infinite wait during attach
body:
Hi Team,

In `od_router_attach()` function if there is a situation when no idle servers are available and no new server connections can be created, in that case co routine is supposed to wait on `od_route_wait` function for infinite large time [here](https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/4f4ff3baa028e793b9926bc65cf58812bfc891e2/sources/router.c#L704). 
I can see the time is configurable using pool_time settings. But can't it land into a situation where no wake up signal is given by the detach phase. Therefore it leads to infinite wait in the od_route_function.
I'm phasing this issue. Wanted to know your thoughts or how can we handle it. 
Thanks

Is odyssey thread safe
body:
Hi Team,
I've broad question regarding the thread safety in odyssey process. As we know odyssey is multi-threaded connection pooler, I'm seeing couple of data race conditions which is leading to odyssey process crash. Some I've listed below. 
I'm definitely using an older version. 
`./build/latest/bin/odyssey --version
odyssey (git: 26399 2.17.3.0-b25_FINAL-9763-gc4b4a52ef0 release)`

But just wanted to confirm have below race conditions been tested or taken into account to ensure thread safety in the latest/stable version of odyssey. 

1. od_route_close() function calls server_free(server), and od_backend_close() also tries to call server_free() directly. 
2. The hashmaps which server or client objects can maintain, I see in some scenarios in hashmap_search() function hashmap is trying to access an element of hashmap which is already free up.
3. Similarly the mm_channel_write(), in which multiple threads were trying to access the same channel simultaneously. 

Thanks

Race Condition while clean up of pools
body:
Hi Team,

I'm witnessing a crash of odyssey process in one of my workloads. I'm using a bit older version of odyssey. I'm attaching below the stack trace. 


thread #1, name = 'odyssey', stop reason = signal SIGSEGV
  frame #0: 0x00005e30f8887c6f odyssey`od_backend_connect(server=0x000032bc7e014380, context="", route_params=0x0000000000000000, client=0x000032bc7da72c00) at backend.c:815:19
  frame #1: 0x00005e30f888580e odyssey`od_frontend_attach(client=0x000032bc7da72c00, context="", route_params=0x0000000000000000) at frontend.c:305:8
  frame #2: 0x00005e30f8881b11 odyssey`od_frontend_remote [inlined] od_frontend_attach_and_deploy(client=0x000032bc7da72c00, context=<unavailable>) at frontend.c:361:11
  frame #3: 0x00005e30f8881afe odyssey`od_frontend_remote(client=0x000032bc7da72c00) at frontend.c:2120:13
  frame #4: 0x00005e30f887dd65 odyssey`od_frontend(arg=0x000032bc7da72c00) at frontend.c:2756:12
  frame #5: 0x00005e30f88a6912 odyssey`mm_scheduler_main(arg=0x000032bc7e7cf900) at scheduler.c:17:2
  frame #6: 0x00005e30f88a6b77 odyssey`mm_context_runner at context.c:28:2


The top of the threads points to: `storage = route->rule->storage;` used in od_router_gc_cb() function. 

I'm suspecting it's happening due to a race condition on how `rule` field of route object is been unref [https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/0856d66419d8cc0a3328fa92f3d463323a55cb22/sources/router.c#L313](here). 
`od_route_unlock(route);

	/* unref route rule and free route object */
	od_rules_unref(route->rule);
	od_route_free(route);`

It releases the lock before doing unref and freeing the route->rule and route object respectively. What if any other worker thread is accessing route->rule after it's been unref in above code after the lock has been released. 

I wanted to confirm, have you guys faced such issue in past or any fixes been done in order to handle the above scenario. 

Thanks!
